elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to each party.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 limits “each Party's total aggregate liability,” making the cap bilateral.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap equals fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 uses “fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: The cap includes a USD 1,000,000 floor.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 contains no USD 1,000,000 minimum or other monetary floor.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the 12-month fee amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The cap is limited solely to the 12-month fee amount and contains no greater-of formulation.

elements.element: Indirect and consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 11.5 provides that “neither Party nor any of its Affiliates” is liable for indirect or consequential damages, among other categories.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 exempts breaches of Article 9 or Section 5.8, but the supplied operative text does not establish that either cross-reference contains confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No express data-protection carve-out appears, and the contents of Article 9 and Section 5.8 are not supplied.

elements.element: Breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No express security carve-out appears, and the contents of Article 9 and Section 5.8 are not supplied.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 expressly excludes “a Party's indemnification obligations under this Article 11” from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 expressly excludes each party's gross negligence from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 expressly excludes willful misconduct from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 expressly excludes fraud from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 contains no express carve-out for infringement of the other party's intellectual property, and the unidentified cross-references do not demonstrate one.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are expressly excluded from “damages” for purposes of the cap.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not state that AbbVie's payment obligations are not damages or otherwise exclude those payment obligations from the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to each party.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 applies to “each Party's total aggregate liability.”

elements.element: The cap is based on fees paid or payable under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 uses fees “paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement” as the cap base.

elements.element: The fee measurement period is the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 expressly uses the “twelve (12) months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 expressly carves out each party's indemnification obligations under Article 11.

elements.evidence: The operative text refers only to Article 9 and Section 5.8; because their contents are not supplied, a confidentiality carve-out cannot be established.

result.reason: The redline creates a mutual 12-month-fees aggregate cap and preserves operative carve-outs for indemnification, fraud, gross negligence, and willful misconduct. It does not satisfy the preferred position because it lacks the USD 1,000,000 floor, data-protection, security, and IP-infringement carve-outs, and the payment-obligations clarification. Neither level can be confirmed because the only possible confidentiality carve-out is through unidentified cross-references to Article 9 or Section 5.8. The drafting is otherwise targeted and does not facially disturb unrelated terms, but the opaque cross-references and undefined treatment of payment obligations materially reduce clarity.
